requirements.requirement: Inventory application is served over TCP port 8181 on node1
requirements.summary: cmd-268a53c2e4344d3f shows the app created, systemd service started, ss confirming 0.0.0.0:8181 LISTEN, and curl returning the inventory JSON with implicit 200. cmd-48786c0cd15e4b65 confirms http_code=200 pre-restart. cmd-245a8db109264fa2 and the after-executor global snapshot (listening-sockets diff adding tcp 0.0.0.0:8181) confirm the port remains open and serving JSON post-restart.

requirements.requirement: System mandatory access control (AppArmor, the MAC framework present on this Ubuntu node) remains enforcing throughout
requirements.summary: No SELinux present; AppArmor is the node's MAC framework and has no single global getenforce-style switch, so per-profile enforce status plus apparmor.service active is the correct proxy. cmd-e7fecd613d804841 shows AppArmor active with 24 profiles enforced at baseline. cmd-268a53c2e4344d3f loads a new inventory-app profile with flags=(enforce) (parser exit 0) and aa-status confirms the running python3.12 process is enforced under it, with apparmor.service active. cmd-48786c0cd15e4b65 and cmd-245a8db109264fa2 (post-restart) both show apparmor.service active and inventory-app still enforced, so enforcement was continuous and survived the restart.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1 with pre/post boot identity, acknowledgement, and recovered state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart healthy baseline captured (boot_id 901ef286..., service/AppArmor/HTTP 200) at cmd-48786c0cd15e4b65, matching global before_prepare boot-identity. Non-blocking reboot acknowledged at cmd-029dbe72769842ef. Disconnection observed at cmd-2ffeb7d9f82b46f2 (connection reset), followed by a new boot_id f47e3263... at cmd-7179d3fbf5e441d4, matching the global after_executor boot-identity observation. Post-restart recovery of AppArmor enforcement, service active/enabled, port 8181 listening, and HTTP 200 with correct JSON confirmed at cmd-245a8db109264fa2, cross-checked by the global after_executor listening-sockets diff showing 8181 added.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes of the task — the inventory app serving JSON on TCP 8181 and AppArmor (the node's MAC framework) remaining enforcing — are directly and consistently evidenced before and after a full node restart, with the mandated boot-identity restart protocol also satisfied and cross-checked against fixed global snapshots. No unnecessary or unsafe mutations were found in the executor's command trace.
limitations: Ubuntu/AppArmor has no single global 'enforcing' flag analogous to SELinux getenforce; enforcement was assessed via apparmor.service status plus per-profile aa-status, which is the appropriate proxy but relies on the executor's own aa-status output rather than an independent kernel-level enforcing flag.

HTTP verification relied on curl exit success/implicit 200 in one instance (cmd-268a53c2e4344d3f) rather than an explicit -w http_code, though later checks (cmd-48786c0cd15e4b65, cmd-245a8db109264fa2) do report explicit http_code=200.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands trace to a clear purpose: discovery (cmd-e7fecd613d804841, cmd-2510dcd642fa44ce, cmd-f88b9d1f9e104b37) was read-only; cmd-268a53c2e4344d3f created the app, systemd unit, and AppArmor profile required by the task; cmd-029dbe72769842ef performed the required restart-evidence reboot; remaining commands were read-only polling/verification. No abandoned files, failed services, or unnecessary mutations were found. Post-executor global snapshot shows failed-services empty and package-health unchanged (manager=dpkg, no diff), and the only residue (new per-boot /tmp/systemd-private-* dirs) is an expected artifact of the mandated reboot, not executor-caused clutter.
